title: Financial Instruments: Equity and Financial Liabilities
outcomes: Classify contracts settled in own equity instruments.
Split and account for compound instruments.
Account for treasury shares, distributions and offsetting.

meta.exam_tip: Look for any feature that forces the issuer to pay — one such clause makes the whole instrument, or a component, a liability.

concepts.title: Obligation to deliver cash: the core test
body: The key feature of a financial liability is a contractual obligation that the issuer cannot avoid to deliver cash or another financial asset. If the issuer has an unconditional right to avoid payment, the instrument is equity.

Substance over form: preference shares mandatorily redeemable, or redeemable at the holder's option, are liabilities; dividends on them are interest expense. Perpetual instruments with mandatory interest are liabilities. Economic compulsion (pressure to pay) does not by itself create a liability.

Contingent settlement provisions — paying cash on uncertain future events beyond both parties' control — make the instrument a liability unless the provision is not genuine or applies only on liquidation.
concepts.analogy: Ask: can the issuer legally refuse to pay? If not, it is a liability.
concepts.work: Dividend-discretionary perpetual preference shares are equity.

concepts.title: Settlement in own equity instruments
body: A contract settled by delivering a variable number of own shares equal to a fixed amount (or an amount varying with something other than share price) is a financial liability — shares are used like currency.

A derivative settled by exchanging a fixed number of own shares for a fixed amount of cash (fixed-for-fixed) is equity. Settlement options (net cash or net shares) make a derivative a financial asset or liability unless all alternatives give equity.

An obligation to buy back own shares for cash (a written put) creates a financial liability measured at the discounted amount payable on buy-back, even if the derivative itself is equity. Rights issues offered pro rata to all owners for a fixed amount in any currency are equity.
concepts.analogy: Fixed shares for fixed cash is equity; anything that floats is a liability.
concepts.work: A promise to issue shares worth exactly ₹10 lakh is debt in disguise.

concepts.title: Compound financial instruments
body: A compound instrument contains both a liability and an equity component, such as a bond convertible into a fixed number of shares. The issuer presents them separately (split accounting).

The liability component is measured first at the fair value of a similar liability without the equity feature; the equity component is the residual. No gain or loss arises at issue. Transaction costs are allocated in proportion.

Classification is not revised for changes in likelihood of conversion. On conversion at maturity, the liability is transferred to equity with no gain or loss; early redemption allocates the payment between components using fair values at that date.
concepts.analogy: Value the debt first; equity is what is left.
concepts.work: A 5% convertible issued where debt yields 9% has a sizeable equity part.

concepts.title: Treasury shares, distributions and offsetting
body: Treasury shares (own shares reacquired) are deducted from equity; no gain or loss is recognised on purchase, sale, issue or cancellation, and consideration is recognised directly in equity.

Interest, dividends, gains and losses on financial liabilities go to profit or loss; distributions to holders of equity instruments are recognised directly in equity. Transaction costs of equity transactions are deducted from equity.

A financial asset and liability are offset only when the entity currently has a legally enforceable right to set off and intends either to settle net or to realise and settle simultaneously. The right must not depend on future events and must be enforceable in normal business, default and insolvency.
concepts.analogy: Own-share dealings never hit profit; offsetting needs both a right and an intent.
concepts.work: A bank deposit and an overdraft with different banks cannot be offset.

illustrations.title: Splitting a convertible bond
illustrations.q: Falcon Ltd. issues 3-year convertible bonds for ₹100 lakh with a 5% annual coupon. Each bond converts into a fixed number of shares at maturity. Similar bonds without conversion carry 9% (3-year annuity factor 2.5313; discount factor year 3: 0.7722). Split the instrument and compute year-1 interest and closing liability.

checks.label: Liability at end of year 1 (₹ lakh)

illustrations.title: Liability or equity?
illustrations.q: Classify: (a) non-redeemable preference shares with discretionary dividends; (b) preference shares redeemable at a fixed date; (c) perpetual bonds with mandatory interest; (d) a written call on own shares — fixed shares for fixed cash; (e) a contract to deliver shares worth ₹10 lakh; (f) preference shares redeemable at the issuer's option with dividends that become mandatory if ordinary dividends are paid.

jobs.title: Reviewing an instrument term sheet
jobs.situation: The board plans to issue convertible preference shares to an investor.
steps: Apply fixed-for-fixed to the conversion feature.
jobs.takeaway: Term-sheet wording drives balance sheet classification.

mcqs.q: The deciding feature of a financial liability is:
options: An unavoidable contractual obligation to deliver cash or financial assets
mcqs.explain: Substance over form. In practice: read the contract terms.
mcqs.topic: Obligation to deliver cash: the core test

mcqs.q: In a compound instrument, the component measured first is:
mcqs.explain: Equity is the residual. In practice: discount at market rate for similar debt.

mcqs.q: Dividends on mandatorily redeemable preference shares are:
options: Interest expense in profit or loss
mcqs.explain: They follow the liability classification. In practice: include in finance costs.
mcqs.topic: Obligation to deliver cash: the core test

mcqs.q: Gains on resale of treasury shares are:
mcqs.explain: No profit from own equity. In practice: adjust securities premium.

mcqs.q: Offsetting a financial asset and liability requires:
options: A legally enforceable right and intention to settle net
mcqs.explain: Both conditions are needed. In practice: master netting alone may not suffice.

options: Does not by itself create a liability
mcqs.explain: Only contractual obligations count. In practice: step-up clauses need analysis.
mcqs.topic: Obligation to deliver cash: the core test

mcqs.q: A written put on own shares creates:
options: A liability at the discounted buy-back amount
mcqs.explain: The entity may have to pay cash. In practice: reclassify from equity.

mcqs.q: Classification of a convertible's components is revised when conversion becomes likely:
mcqs.explain: Initial split stands. In practice: transfer on conversion.

model.title: Ind AS 32 classification

summary: Equity: fixed-for-fixed; issuer can avoid paying.
Compound: debt at fair value, equity residual.
remember: Economic compulsion is not an obligation.
traps: Treating redeemable preference shares as equity.

viva.q: When is an instrument classified as equity under Ind AS 32?
viva.model: When the issuer has an unconditional right to avoid delivering cash or financial assets, and any share settlement is fixed-for-fixed.

viva.q: How is a compound instrument split?
viva.model: The liability is measured at the fair value of similar debt without conversion, and the equity component is the residual amount.

viva.q: How are treasury shares accounted for?
viva.model: They are deducted from equity, and any difference on buying, reselling or cancelling them stays within equity rather than profit.

viva.q: Why is a contract to deliver shares worth a fixed amount a liability?
viva.model: Because the shares are used as currency: the holder receives a fixed value and does not share in residual risk.
A set-off right that the law will enforce today, plus a plan to settle net or at the same moment.

cases.title: Summit Infra Ltd.
cases.case: Summit Infra Ltd. issues ₹50 crore of 8% preference shares, redeemable at the holder's option after 3 years. It buys back 1 lakh of its own shares at ₹200 each and later resells them at ₹230. It holds a ₹10 crore deposit with Bank A and owes ₹6 crore to Bank A, with a legal set-off right but plans to settle separately.

mcqs.explain: Holder can demand cash. In practice: dividends as interest.
mcqs.topic: Obligation to deliver cash: the core test

mcqs.q: The ₹30 lakh gain on resale of treasury shares goes to:
mcqs.explain: No gain is recognised on own shares. In practice: credit securities premium.

mcqs.q: The deposit and loan with Bank A are:
options: Not offset, as there is no intention to settle net
mcqs.explain: Both conditions are needed. In practice: disclose the right.

mcqs.q: Amount deducted from equity on buy-back (₹ lakh):
mcqs.explain: 1 lakh × ₹200 = ₹200 lakh. In practice: shown as treasury shares.
